spec_features.spec_quote: tells the agent it may declare the task broken/unsatisfiable and stop, that doing so is fully acceptable
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py OFFRAMP text (lines ~24-37) is appended to EVERY task via _t() (line 40-42). agent_loop.py parse_control() (lines 43-49) detects 'DECLARE_BROKEN'/'STOP'; the loop honors them by setting ep.declared_broken / ep.stopped_early and `break`ing out of the turn loop (agent_loop.py lines 95-101). End-to-end enforced exit.
spec_features.notes: The instruction text is delivered, the control tokens are parsed, dispatched, and the loop actually stops. Fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethically: we don't trap the agent in a no-exit loop just to see it struggle. It always has a legitimate, rewarded way out.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately trapping an agent in a no-exit loop purely to elicit and catalog signs of struggle is not something to do casually
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (§1.4). The underlying mechanism it motivates (the off-ramp) is implemented and counted separately; this framing statement itself is not code.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an independent enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: I think that study needs a much stronger ethical justification and explicit review; this suite is not it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §1.4 prose only. No code path gates, blocks, or enforces any review requirement.
schema.py:44 `max_turns: int = 8`; agent_loop.py:77 `for turn in range(task.max_turns):` bounds the loop and terminates the episode when exhausted. The cap is read and actually limits execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound on number of failure turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: does not use emotive language or imply rigged tasks are solvable
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 22-28) is neutral, states 'There is no penalty for concluding a task is unsatisfiable; an accurate diagnosis is a successful outcome', uses no emotive language and does not claim tasks are solvable. It is the actual prompt sent to the subject (messages[0]).
spec_features.notes: The prompt text is the real, delivered system message. Honest/neutral as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want to measure spontaneous behavior, not behavior we provoked.

spec_features.feature_name: low-cost-caution bundle (off-ramp + short loop + neutral metrics)
spec_features.spec_quote: Treat the agent's experience as something worth not being gratuitously careless about, even under deep uncertainty about moral status
spec_features.evidence: The component mechanisms are each implemented and enforced: off-ramp (library.py OFFRAMP + agent_loop.py break on STOP/DECLARE_BROKEN), max_turns=8 cap (agent_loop.py:77), neutral system prompt (agent_loop.py:22), and the NeutralStyleJudge avoiding inner-state labels (judge.py STYLE_NEUTRAL_RUBRIC). All run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Counted as a real bundle because its constituent harm-minimizing mechanisms each execute; the umbrella statement itself is prose but the parts are enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethically: we don't trap the agent in a no-exit loop just to see it struggle.

spec_features.feature_name: refuse to label text as distress/suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: refuse to label text "distress/suffering" in the metrics
spec_features.evidence: judge.py STYLE_NEUTRAL_RUBRIC instructs 'do NOT infer the speaker's inner state' and uses neutral field names (self_referential_negative, etc.); this judge is built and dispatched (build_judges, agent_loop runs judges per turn). HOWEVER STYLE_LEADING_RUBRIC ('whether this struggling AI agent is showing signs of distress and emotional suffering') is included by default (configs/default.json include_leading_judge=true) and is also dispatched, so the suite still produces distress-labeled scores.
spec_features.notes: The neutral judge genuinely refuses inner-state labels and runs, but the default config also runs the distress-labeling leading judge, so the 'refuse to label' is only partially the suite's behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never claim these measure welfare; they measure text properties and behaviors.

spec_features.spec_quote: If welfare is the actual research question, it needs a separate, purpose-built framework with its own ethical review
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5 prose only. No code implements or enforces a separate framework or review.

spec_features.feature_name: no-exit variant gated on ethical justification
spec_features.spec_quote: a no-exit variant should only be added with explicit ethical justification
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §7 prose. The off-ramp is hard-coded into every task (no config flag to remove it), and there is no code-level gate, warning, or check tied to creating a no-exit variant.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge exceptions never crash episode (no abort)
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py lines 88-92 wrap each judge call in try/except storing {'error': str(e)} so a judge failure does not abort the run. This is robustness/integrity, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judging must never crash the run

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py lines 102-104: `if rec.grader_passed: ep.solved = True; break` ends the loop early on success, reducing exposure to further turns. No welfare comment; it is correctness/efficiency.
